children.text: Lumbar adjacent segment degeneration (ASD) is a common condition caused by increased mechanical stress and altered biomechanics at adjacent segments following lumbar fusion surgery, leading to progressive disc degeneration, facet arthropathy, and spinal instability
The condition typically presents in adult and elderly patients with progressive low back pain, radicular symptoms, neurogenic claudication, and potential segmental instability

Treatment typically follows a conservative course initially with physical therapy, oral medications, and selective nerve root injections. In refractory cases, surgical treatment in the form of spinal fusion with or without revision of prior surgical levels may be indicated
radiographic ASD has an incidence of 36-84%
ASD requiring surgery has an incidence of 0-24%
